problem_summary.summary: Return the nonnegative integer square root of x, rounded down, without using a built-in power operation.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a nonnegative 32-bit integer x. Return floor(sqrt(x)).
constraints: Do not use a built-in exponent function or operator

brute_force.explanation: Try positive integers in ascending order until the next square would exceed x. Use a long multiplication so the comparison itself cannot overflow.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The square function is increasing for nonnegative integers. The final candidate whose square is at most x is therefore the greatest integer satisfying the required floor-square-root condition.

optimized.explanation: Binary-search the integer range for the greatest value whose square is at most x. Compare mid with x / mid instead of multiplying, avoiding overflow.
optimized.correctness_idea: For positive mid, mid <= x / mid is equivalent to mid squared <= x. This predicate is true up to the floor square root and false afterward, so binary search finds the boundary.
optimized.time_complexity: O(log x) for x > 0; O(1) for x = 0.

steps.action: Discard mid and all larger candidates by setting high to 18.
Discard 9 and larger values by setting high to 8.
Record answer 4 and search higher values.
Record answer 6 and search above it.
Set high to 6; the search ends and answer 6 is returned.

edge_cases.handling: The binary-search loop is skipped and answer 0 is returned.
The only positive candidate 1 satisfies the division comparison.
The exact root satisfies the predicate and is recorded as the maximum valid candidate.
The optimized comparison uses division, not a potentially overflowing square.
